# The studio
_Source: closefuture-profile.pdf › The studio_

An agency built for speed
Where a traditional shop takes months, CloseFuture measures the gap between an idea and a
shipped product in weeks.
CloseFuture calls itself an AI product studio, and the label is earned. The team compresses the usual
build cycle by leaning on modern low-code platforms and AI-assisted development — without letting
quality slip. The products they hand over aren't throwaway prototypes; they run in production with
payments, notifications, role-based access and automation already wired in.
Two kinds of clients tend to find them. Founders come to validate an idea quickly and get a polished MVP
in front of real users on a lean budget. Enterprises come for secure, scalable tools and AI features they
need faster than an in-house roadmap allows. In both cases the studio behaves less like a vendor and
more like an extension of the client's own team — a point that comes up again and again in reviews.
"They never say 'not possible' — they figure it out." — verified client review

# Founder and contact
_Source: closefuture-profile.pdf › Founder and contact_

Founder — and the person clients actually talk to.
CloseFuture is led by Baskaran Manimohan, who also runs the personal brand Baskaran Builds and
is a familiar name in the low-code and AI development community. He stays close to delivery: in client
reviews, "Baskaran" is the contact named for responsiveness, hands-on involvement and clear
communication.
His path runs through the heart of the no-code movement — time in and around Bubble, Era of No
Code and GrowthX — sharpened by an IIT Patna generative-AI certification and study at
EDHEC Business School. He often mentions growing up in a small village in India, which shapes the
studio's guiding idea: high-quality product development should be fast and affordable enough for anyone
with a good idea.

UGC MARKETPLACE · ISRAEL · 2026
Dipy — a marketplace for user-generated content
Dipy is an Israeli marketplace that connects brand owners with content creators. Brands post orders for
videos, photos or graphics; creators browse, apply, produce the work and get paid. Simple on the surface
— but the market it entered was anything but.
THE PROBLEM
Existing UGC solutions were fragmented. A brand wanting content had to stitch together separate tools
for discovering creators, running quality assurance, managing revisions, handling payments and staying
compliant on the legal side. Creators had it no easier — there was no single place to find good
opportunities and keep an eye on what they were actually earning.
WHAT CLOSEFUTURE BUILT
A production-grade platform on Bubble, split into four purpose-built surfaces so each user gets exactly
the interface they need:
Brand-owner desktop — a command hub for creating orders, searching the creator database,
sending direct invitations and tracking everything in flight.
Content-creator mobile — a native-feeling interface tuned to a 420px width, for browsing orders,
applying, uploading work, handling revisions and tracking earnings.
Brand-owner mobile — a touch-optimized version for managing orders and talking to creators on
the go.
Admin panel — creator verification, order oversight and payment processing for the operations
team.
THE DETAILS THAT MATTERED
AI semantic search matching creators to orders by language, interests and personal characteristics —
cutting the time brands spend choosing.
Full bilingual support in Hebrew and English.
Automated payments handling VAT, discount codes and partial credits.
Notifications across four channels: push, in-app messaging, WhatsApp and email.
A creator level-progression system that unlocks higher-value opportunities over time.
Direct creator invitations running alongside organic applications.
Outcome — Dipy launched as a production marketplace handling hundreds of concurrent orders,
with approvals and payments running largely on their own.

EMPLOYEE WELLBEING · AI · 2026
Liya AI — a wellbeing platform that listens
Liya AI is an intelligent employee-wellbeing platform for stress management. It blends conversational AI,
real-time surveys and analytics with access to real human therapists — automation where it helps, people
where it matters.
THE PROBLEM
Organizations couldn't see stress and burnout building until it was too late. Traditional surveys arrived
too slowly to act on. Employees held back for fear of being identified. And HR teams had no realistic way
to read and act on large volumes of open feedback.
WHAT CLOSEFUTURE BUILT
Liya Coach — a conversational AI assistant supporting both text and voice, so employees can raise
concerns in whatever way feels safe.
Survey management — tools to create and send surveys that capture mood and engagement in real
time.
Voice-enabled interaction — natural-language input for intuitive, low-friction use.
Automated summarization — AI that turns raw survey data into clear, actionable insight.
Analytics dashboard — interactive visual reporting with advanced filters for spotting trends across
teams and segments.
The platform ships as both web and mobile applications, and was completed in 2026.
Outcome — better visibility into wellbeing and faster, data-driven decisions. Voice and chat
pushed participation up, while therapist integration kept the support genuinely personal — feeding
into higher satisfaction and a healthier workplace.

SMART OFFICE · IOT · ISRAEL · 2026
Webiz — the oﬃce, on demand
Webiz lets professionals and companies book premium offices and meeting rooms by the hour, with no
long-term contract. What makes it interesting is that the software reaches past the screen and into the
building itself.
THE PROBLEM
Traditional office rentals are rigid, expensive and a poor fit for how people actually work now. Companies
pay for space that sits empty, and juggle access, scheduling and billing across systems that don't talk to
each other.
WHAT CLOSEFUTURE BUILT
A complete ecosystem — a mobile app, an admin dashboard and an on-site tablet application — sitting on
a backend that unifies discovery, booking, payments and device control into one flow:
QR-code instant booking — tablets on site show codes for immediate access and real-time
availability checks.
Flexible scheduling — hourly, future-dated, extended and permanent bookings.
Company wallet — a shared team credit pool with member management.
Dynamic pricing — bonus credit packages, per-order discounts and auto-renewal.
Secure payments — integrated through Rivhit.
IoT control — automated doors, electricity and air-conditioning, all from the app.
Outcome — launched July 2026 in Israel, turning rigid office rentals into flexible, self-service
access and automating what used to be manual building management.

# More shipped products
_Source: closefuture-profile.pdf › More shipped products_

Three more shipped products
SPEED DATING · 2025
Randevmeste
A platform for offline speed-dating events where guests meet up to 30 matches a night in short
rounds. The client had outgrown a Wix-only setup with no guest tracking, real-time
communication, filtering or notifications.
What CloseFuture built. A custom Bubble app integrated with Wix over API — tickets bought
on Wix flow straight into the database. Guests register by ticket number, build profiles, and move
through event phases with real-time liking and matching, instant match alerts, secure post-event
messaging, safety tools, and host controls.
"The app has exceeded our expectations both in terms of design and functionality." — Jozef
Greftak, client
WOMEN'S FITNESS · 2025
Vigo
A fitness app built specifically for women — personalized workouts, meal tracking and AI nutrition
analysis — because generic fitness apps miss the mark on personalization and motivation.
What CloseFuture built. Goal-based onboarding and plans; real-time activity/calorie tracking
that adjusts dynamically; custom diet plans with portion guidance; AI meal analysis through a
WhatsApp bot (log a meal with a photo); and subscriptions via RevenueCat. Launched 2025 in
Israel, with strong retention.
CREATOR COMMUNITY · 2025
Galaxy Move
A mobile-first community platform connecting Samsung creators and fans through gamified
engagement, built because existing tools lacked interactivity and scale.
What CloseFuture built. A gamified task-and-points system, community posting with direct
admin contact, a real-time leaderboard, role-based admin controls (super admins vs. limited
community managers), and reward redemption for gifts and coupons. Delivered as mobile and web
apps, boosting engagement and brand loyalty.

From the blog
Founder-written pieces on platform choices, scaling and enterprise readiness.
Building scalable apps with FlutterFlow
21 May 2026
A guide to architecting FlutterFlow apps that grow from MVP to thousands of users. The core argument:
scalability is a shared job between a strong backend (Supabase, Firebase or custom APIs doing the heavy
lifting) and a disciplined frontend. It walks through backend-first architecture, clean relational data
models, pagination and lazy loading, consistent naming, careful state management, reusable
components, and row-level security — the difference between a demo and something production-ready.
Neon vs Supabase: a 2026 choosing & migration guide
29 April 2026
A practical comparison of two Postgres platforms: Neon, a serverless database with autoscaling and
branching, versus Supabase, a full backend bundling auth, storage, realtime and auto-generated APIs.
The piece weighs authentication, realtime, branching, scale-to-zero economics and pricing, then lands on
a clear rule of thumb — Neon for composable, bursty, ephemeral setups; Supabase for fast MVPs and
standard SaaS — and notes that migrating between them is easy in theory but 1–3 weeks of real work.
Top Framer agencies in Dubai (2026)
7 July 2026
A curated look at the Framer agencies serving Dubai's startup scene with fast, conversion-focused sites.
It's one entry in a wider regional series that also covers Riyadh, along with n8n automation roundups for
Germany, France, Spain and Poland, and platform guides for Lovable and FlutterFlow across the UAE
and India.
FlutterFlow for Enterprise: can it handle large-scale apps?
21 May 2026
A companion to the scalability piece, this article tackles the question enterprises actually ask before
committing to a low-code platform: will it hold up? It examines FlutterFlow's viability for enterprise
deployments across the dimensions that decide it — scalability, performance, third-party integrations and
security — arguing that with the right backend and architecture, low-code is a legitimate choice well
beyond the MVP stage.

A run of location- and platform-specific roundups aimed at founders searching for the right build
partner: top n8n automation agencies in Germany, France, Spain and Poland; Framer studios in Dubai
